title: Top Secret
paragraphs: A 1950 espionage series starring Ilona Massey as Baroness Karen Gaza, placing its heroine in stories of international intrigue and intelligence work connected with Europe and World War II.

NBC sustaining espionage drama starring Ilona Massey as Baroness Karen Geza/Gayzer. Historical run contains 19 numbered assignments. Frozen 19 objects represent 16 unique assignments plus three alternate dramatic/rehearsal manifestations; assignments 5, 12 and 13 are absent from the frozen subset.

GRH documents the program through Monday opening period (June 12, 1950 to July 10, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Sunday period (July 23, 1950 to August 20, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], Friday period (September 1, 1950 to September 8, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Monday return (September 18, 1950 to September 25, 1950) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Ilona Massey (performer on 19 recordings), Fred Collins (announcer on 6 recordings), Harry W. Junkin (writer on 6 recordings, director on 2 recordings, and producer on 2 recordings), Roy Shield (composer on 5 recordings and conductor on 5 recordings), Allan Stevenson (performer on 2 recordings), Brook Byron (performer on 2 recordings), and Luis Van Rooten (performer on 2 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include international espionage, World War II intelligence operations, counterintelligence and undercover identity, sabotage and counter-sabotage, and rehearsal and transcription preservation.
GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including World War II espionage setting, Transcribed/rehearsal preservation, and NBC summer Top Secret run.
